variants.stem: Which one of the following patient’s characteristics need to do further work up for secondary hypertension?

options.text: 20 Year old gentleman with family history of pheochromocytoma
60 Year old gentleman with Blood pressure 120/80 on three antihypertensive  medications
20 Year old gentleman with blood pressure 165/95
60 Year old lady with blood pressure 145/85 on two antihypertensive medications

variants.aiSuggestion: Reference answer retained; individual medical verification is pending.
variants.explanation: The recorded answers conflict with the clinical indications. A family history of pheochromocytoma and severe hypertension at age 20 both warrant evaluation for a secondary cause; option A is the strongest single red flag, while option B also merits work-up. A normotensive 60-year-old does not.

variants.aiSuggestion: Reference answer retained; individual medical verification is pending.
variants.explanation: This patient has severe pneumonia with shock, hypoxemia, confusion, multilobar infiltrates, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and renal dysfunction. ICU admission is the appropriate level of care, so B is the expected answer; the bank's A/B conflict is retained rather than silently changed.

lectureEvidence.title: L3) Community Acquired Pneumonia
lectureEvidence.quote: Minor (need≥3) RR ≥30 PaO2/FiO2 ≤250 (2) Multilobar infiltrates Confusion Uremia (BUN ≥20) (Acute Kidney Injury) Leukopenia (3) Thrombocytopenia (4) Hypothermia
lectureEvidence.statement: The lecture lists severe-CAP minor criteria, including tachypnea, confusion and uremia, with three or more required. Clinical ICU assessment is separate from simply reciting the list.
lectureEvidence.note: The clinical interpretation applies this teaching to the case; it is separate from the original lecture wording.

variants.stem: A 30 year old male patient, presented with worsening lower limb edema for 5 days which started suddenly. His blood pressure is 200/65. Serum creatinine is 55 McMillan/L (normal). Which of the following is the likely cause?
variants.aiSuggestion: The available stem/options do not establish a single defensible answer; see the medical review below.
variants.explanation: Membranous nephropathy. is the keyed answer and is the option most consistent with the information provided. Glomerular disease is separated into nephritic and nephrotic patterns using hematuria, proteinuria, kidney function, urine sediment, and systemic features.

lectureEvidence.note: No supporting original-lecture passage has been verified for this question. No lecture page is claimed; the clinical interpretation is separate.

variants.reviewOpinion: Sudden edema with normal creatinine does not distinguish MN from MCD or other causes. Urinalysis, protein quantification, albumin and etiological clues are missing.
